name: Tender and Easy Buttermilk Waffles
headnote: Diana Perry's note is brief: she wanted waffles that come out crisp outside and tender inside without the fuss of separating eggs and beating the whites, and she points out they reheat well in a toaster for weekday mornings. The site adds that the batter comes together fast and that members like how quickly the waffles crisp back up in a toaster oven. There is no real technique discussion beyond stirring the wet into the dry only until the batter is still slightly lumpy.
comment_digest: The top review (84 helpful, Sarah Jo) found the batter too thin when doubled and added an extra cup of all-purpose flour; she also used half whole wheat, which made the waffles sturdier. Thin batter is the recurring complaint, and others likewise add about half a cup more flour, sometimes with cream of tartar and cinnamon; a few go the other way and thin it further for upright irons. Half whole wheat flour is the most-reported substitution and works well, as does a 1-to-1 gluten-free flour blend (one reviewer used 280 g) with no added gum. Without buttermilk, people substitute 1/3 cup Greek yogurt or sour cream plus 2/3 cup milk per cup. Doubling the vanilla, or adding almond extract or cinnamon, is a common flavour tweak. On doneness, one reviewer warns to pull the waffles at medium brown, since going darker dries them out and toughens them; another reported them going dark before crisping.
